::: {.callout-important}
## Warning — Uncalibrated Model
This is the **Phase 1 (Walking Skeleton)** version of the report. The network
geometry comes straight from raw OSM data and demand is entirely **hypothetical**
(engineering guesswork, not field data). Results here are valid **only for
testing the reproducible pipeline end-to-end** — not for any scenario
comparison or absolute-value prediction. Scenario comparison and sensitivity
analysis follow in Phases 2-4, once accurate geometry and evidence-based demand
are in place.
:::

## 1. Purpose of this version

Per the project roadmap (`CLAUDE.md`), Phase 1's goal is a **complete,
end-to-end** pipeline — from raw OSM data to a published report — even with raw
geometry and demand. This report demonstrates pipeline correctness, not final
engineering findings.

## 2. Network construction and grade-separation check

The network was built from OpenStreetMap (Overpass API, bbox around the Seyedi
under-bridge intersection) using `netconvert`. Separation between the elevated
bridge deck (Imam Reza Highway, `bridge=yes layer=1`) and the at-grade network
below (Seyedi road / Shahid Soleimani Blvd) was **visually inspected and
confirmed** (@fig-layer-check) — per `CLAUDE.md` this is the single most
critical failure point for this model.

![Visual grade-separation check: red = bridge deck (z>0), blue = at-grade network (z=0). The deck passes over the ground network with no connection.](../outputs/figures/network_layer_check_zoom.png){#fig-layer-check width=85%}

## 3. Demand: the jtrrouter method

Per `CLAUDE.md`'s methodology justification, for a single intersection, entry
volume per approach + turning ratios is far less data-hungry than a full OD
matrix. Demand in this version is entirely hypothetical (see
`config/assumptions.yml`, sections `demand_baseline_phase1` and
`traffic_control.turn_ratio_baseline`):

| Approach | Hypothetical entry volume (veh/h) |
|---|---|
| West (bridge deck) | 800 |
| East (bridge deck) | 800 |
| North (Seyedi road) | 500 |
| South (Shahid Soleimani Blvd) | 500 |

## 4. Run result (single seed, S0 scenario)

```{python}
#| label: tbl-kpi
#| tbl-cap: "KPI summary by approach — scenario S0, single seed=42"
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("../outputs/tables/s0_kpi_summary.csv")
df.columns = ["Approach", "N vehicles", "Mean duration (s)",
              "Mean time loss (s)", "Mean waiting (s)", "Mean route length (m)"]
from IPython.display import Markdown
Markdown(df.round(2).to_markdown(index=False))
```

![Mean time loss by approach (single seed, hypothetical demand)](../outputs/figures/s0_timeloss_by_approach.png){#fig-timeloss width=85%}

All 2,600 generated vehicles entered the network and completed their trips (no
gridlock or routing failures) — a basic health signal for network connectivity
and routing. Time-loss values are low in this run because current hypothetical
demand is fairly light; this number carries **no engineering meaning** until
real demand (Phase 3) replaces it.

## 5. Limitations of this version

- Intersection geometry comes directly from OSM; imagery-based corrections
  (exact lane counts, turning radii, pier positions) have not been applied yet
  (Phase 2).
- Demand and turning ratios are entirely hypothetical (Phase 3).
- Only one scenario (S0) and one seed were run; **no scenario comparison can be
  drawn from this report** — per the project's Hard Rule 5.
- The fleet is homogeneous (passenger cars only); motorcycle share and the
  sublane model are added in Phase 2.
- The Persian report currently uses Quarto's default theme (the Vazirmatn font
  and full RTL/xepersian layout are finalized in Phase 5).
